name: default
based_on: Splink 5 Getting Started, 'Simple Splink Model Example' (the fake_1000 persons model): comparisons, blocking, training steps, the predict cutoff and the 0.95 clustering threshold as documented
changes_from_doc: DateOfBirthComparison('dob') and the blocking rule block_on('first_name', 'dob') are dropped: the pages carry no date of birth
first_name and surname are the first and last words of the page title; email is the first listed email; values are not cleaned (the example's data is already clean)
proposed_note: none: Splink documents no clerical-review band (its threshold guides say to pick a threshold from labelled data), so the default config has no proposed tier

companies.based_on: These company mappings are ours: the tool's documentation has no company example, so each person field is mapped to the company field that plays the same part. This section maps the Getting Started persons model (the people config above) onto company pages, keeping its shape: one name comparison, city with term-frequency adjustments, one contact key, one blocking rule, the same training steps, predict cutoff and 0.95 threshold
changes_from_doc: ours: NameComparison('first_name') and JaroAtThresholds('surname') become one JaroAtThresholds on the whole company name (name_concat), because a company name has no forename and surname

ours: EmailComparison('email') becomes ExactMatch('domain'), the first listed domain, because a domain is the company's contact key as an email is a person's; world.py builds the domains from the domain field and the website host
ExactMatch('city') with term-frequency adjustments is kept as documented
ours: the blocking rule block_on('surname') becomes block_on('first_word'), the first word of the name, because a company name's last word is often a legal suffix
ours: the training blocks (first_name, surname) and (email) become (name_concat) and (domain)
values are not cleaned, as in the people config
